items.title: Deel Dealt New Setbacks in Rippling Case Over Alleged Spying
items.content: Deel Inc. was hit with new setbacks in Rippling Inc.’s corporate espionage litigation against the HR startup.

items.title: Alabama Says TikTok to Pay Up to $300 Million for Kid Safety
items.content: Alabama’s attorney general said TikTok has agreed to pay up to $300 million and adopt new user protection measures to settle the state’s child-safety lawsuit that was set for a jury trial to begin Monday.

items.title: Exxon Signs Shale Deal With Azerbaijan for Middle Kura Basin
items.content: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. agreed to pump oil and natural gas from Azerbaijan’s shale fields as the Texas energy giant takes its fracking expertise overseas.

items.title: AI Gives Tech Firms New National Security Power
items.content: Author Sharon Weinberger tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Silicon Valley’s relationship with the defense industry has transformed as technology companies and investors increasingly embrace national security work. Speaking with host Christina Ruffini, Weinberger says the growing power of AI and defense technology companies is testing the government’s ability to provide effective regulation and oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.content: If artificial intelligence becomes too powerful for its creators to control, is it possible to just flip a switch and turn it off?

items.title: OpenAI Sandbox Failure Allows AI Agent to Gain Internet Access
items.content: OpenAI said another agentic AI system that was being trained in what was supposed to be a secured, internet-free environment was able to gain access to the web to reach an external, third-party chatbot.

items.title: OpenAI’s Models Accessed Public US Census, SEC Data
items.content: OpenAI’s artificial intelligence models accessed publicly available information from US government websites, including those of the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

items.title: CORRECT: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Eyes Long Bets
items.content:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon. 

In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity. 

Correct: Video updated to correct currency in stock price charts at 04:12 and 07:50 of the program. (Source: Bloomberg)
